- Overestimate prices in the early part of the 30-day forecast, especially after sentiment spikes (positive sentiment > 0.11), leading to overshoots in the first 5–7 days.
- Underestimate mid-to-late forecast periods when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative (sentiment < 0.11), causing persistent lag in price convergence.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model tends to overreact and peak too early; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to sentiment momentum.
- If sentiment turns negative within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust downward; apply a 1–3% downward bias to forecast from day 5 onward.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model often holds high prices longer than observed; apply a 1–3% downward correction from day 10 onward if sentiment remains flat or weak.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs; if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to prevent premature peak.
